dimensions.label: Economic model
dimensions.description: Reads the proposed role of markets, public investment, taxation and redistribution. All reviewed programmes contain mixed policies; this is an editorial reading, not a measured ideology.
rubric: Explicit balance of market and state
Redistribution and public services take the lead
Structural redistribution and public economic institutions

dimensions.label: Social protection
dimensions.description: Distinguishes benefits aimed at selected eligible households from explicit commitments to universal rights. More spending does not by itself mean more universality.
rubric: Explicit balance of targeted and universal provision

dimensions.label: Family law
dimensions.description: Based on dated positions on inheritance, legal guardianship, polygamy and marriage. This is not a score of religiosity or the whole party platform.
rubric: Defends existing religious inheritance and marital restrictions
Explicit compromise on the selected questions
Broad equal-rights reform across the selected questions

dimensions.label: Religion & civil law
dimensions.description: Uses the concrete debate over Article 400 of the Family Code. Keeping a religious reference is coded negative; removing it is positive. This narrow indicator does not establish support for or opposition to full institutional secularism.
rubric: Explicitly proposes removing the religious fallback

dimensions.label: Civil liberties
dimensions.description: Uses explicit programme proposals on peaceful assembly, speech, detention and privacy. Silence is unknown, not a centrist position.
rubric: Proposes broad protections and reversals of restrictions

dimensions.label: Strike rights
dimensions.description: A dated, narrow indicator based on responses to law 97.15. Committee responses are not individual plenary roll calls and do not describe every labour policy.
rubric: Opposed restrictions in the reviewed record
Explicitly commits to reversing the framework
